question: Where can I get the road network (geometry) of the United States, with road category, owner and traffic volume (annual average daily traffic)?

answer.summary: FHWA's Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) is the national source: state-reported section lines for public roads, each with functional system (f_system), legal owner (ownership) and AADT. BTS serves it as per-state, per-year ArcGIS services (52 jurisdictions) and FHWA as one 2025 table (17,361,652 rows). Codes are numeric and decoded in the Field Manual. AADT is required only on Federal-aid roads; local roads rarely have it. Count stations come from state GIS (Caltrans: state highways only).
main_caveats: Rows are linear-referenced sections, not roads or count stations. Row counts change by year and state (CA 958,293 in 2024 vs 803,191 in 2025); the README admits overlapping and gapped geometry.
AADT is bidirectional on two-way sections and directional on one-way roads and ramps. Growth factors may be applied to older counts, so data_year is not the count year.
AADT is required only on Federal-aid highways: CA 2024 has it on 21 of 488,722 local rows, DE 2025 on 23,276 of 65,459. Rural minor collectors are also often missing.
f_system and ownership are integer codes with no domains in the services. Decode them with the Field Manual (the DOI resolves to the December 2016 edition; errata exist).
The 2025 README flags North Dakota and New Jersey as missing substantial portions of data. The shortfall was not measured here.
fhwa.dot.gov and highways.dot.gov pages refused default curl requests (403). Data services, GitHub and data.transportation.gov were reachable.
answer.confidence_reason: Services and queries were tested for DE and CA and cross-checked with Caltrans 2024; other states were only counted and the 47 GB national file was not downloaded.

attributes.note: Section polylines (WGS84) for public roads, by state and year or as one 2025 national table. The 2025 README flags North Dakota and New Jersey as substantially incomplete.
attributes.gap_note: The 2025 README says ND and NJ miss substantial portions and that overlaps and gaps exist; the size of the shortfall was not measured here. DE and CA were queried; other states were only counted.

attributes.note: f_system 1-7 (Interstate to Local) is the functional class; route_signing, route_number and nhs hold administrative designations. Code meanings are only in the Field Manual.
ownership is a numeric legal-owner code (1 State Highway Agency, 4 City or Municipal, 80 Other...) for all public roads; maintenance_operations is a separate field.
aadt is attached to sections with data_year; HPMS has no station id. Caltrans publishes count stations (points, back/ahead AADT, 2024) for state highways only.
attributes.gap_note: AADT is required only on Federal-aid highways. CA 2024: AADT on 21 of 488,722 local rows; DE 2025: 23,276 of 65,459. Local-road counts sit with cities, counties or states; other states were not measured.

how_to_use.example_result: 2 features, first: route_id KC-00150-F, route_name SR1N, begin_point 12.87, end_point 12.92, f_system 2, ownership 1, facility_type 2, aadt 54598, data_year 2025, aadt_vd 2025-01-01; polyline of 3 vertices near -75.5823, 39.2724.
steps: List services at https://geo.dot.gov/server/rest/services/Hosted?f=pjson and pick HPMS_FULL_<ST>_<YYYY> (two-letter state code, data year).
Count with query?where=1%3D1&returnCountOnly=true&f=json; maxRecordCount is 2000, so page with resultOffset and resultRecordCount.
Filter by f_system, ownership or route_number and request outSR=4326 geometry (the layer is in WGS84).
Decode f_system and ownership with the HPMS Field Manual code tables; the service has no coded-value domains.
Treat aadt as per section: bidirectional on two-way roads, directional on one-way roads and ramps; check data_year and facility_type.
reading_traps: Counts are sections, not roads: DE had 76,546 rows in 2024 and 94,749 in 2025; CA had 958,293 and 803,191. Do not compare years or states by row count.
Field names change between years: HPMS_FULL_CA_2024 uses routenumber and sectionlength; DE and CA 2025 use route_number and section_length.
aadt is empty on many rows: DE 2025 has it on 47,556 of 94,749 rows (23,276 of 65,459 local rows); CA 2024 has it on 21 of 488,722 local rows.
The README for 2024 linked from data.gov points to a GitHub branch that returns 404; the READMEs now sit under main/HPMS_Metadata/<year>/.
Overlapping features with different route IDs exist, mostly on roads not owned by a state; summing section_length can double count.

problems: The FeatureServer layers expose f_system and ownership as plain integers without coded-value domains.
Field naming differs between years (2024 CA layer vs 2025 layers).
The HPMS README linked from the data.gov record returns 404 (wrong branch name).

steps: Count rows with https://data.transportation.gov/resource/6uzi-vq42.json?$select=count(*) (returned 17361652, equal to the README).
Filter with $where on stateid, f_system, ownership or county_id; note that stateid is numeric but route_number is text.
Use $limit and $offset to page; the export of the whole table is about 47 GB per the README, so prefer filtered queries or a state service.
Decode codes with the HPMS Field Manual; values come back as strings in JSON.
reading_traps: Column names differ from the BTS state services (stateid, year_record, routename here; state_id, data_year, route_name there).
Numbers arrive as strings in the SODA JSON response.
The README's summary line says generated 2025-10-08 but its citation says 2026-10-08.
Sampled items such as curves or grades describe the whole sample section, not the homogeneous piece.

problems: A HEAD request on the GeoJSON export returned Content-Length 0; the full file was not downloaded.
The SODA endpoint returns attribute strings and a line column; typing differs from the BTS services.

open_questions: Which AADT values are counts of the data year and which are growth-adjusted? Starting point: Field Manual metadata (AADT_Growth) and the HPMS data-access story at https://data.transportation.gov/stories/s/3uu4-47sa (page returned 200; contents not read). Next step: read the story's metadata tables.

How large is the North Dakota and New Jersey shortfall flagged in the 2025 README? Starting point: HPMS_FULL_ND_2025 (103,400 rows) and HPMS_FULL_NJ_2025 (159,683 rows). Next step: compare summed section length with each state's public road mileage.

Which Field Manual edition and errata apply to the 2025 codes? Starting point: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/ and its errata page (403 to curl). Next step: open them with a different legitimate client or an archived copy.
How common is local-road AADT in other states? Starting point: group-by statistics on f_system with where=aadt IS NOT NULL, run on CA 2024 and DE 2025. Next step: repeat on the other state services.

How many OSM highway ways carry operator tags? Starting point: the Overpass count for the Delaware bounding box (two attempts returned 502). Next step: retry with a smaller area or another Overpass instance.
